method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW 'Non small cell lung cancer locally advanced or metastatic osimertinib (eviQ ID 1996 v.5)' (ID 1996 v.5; first approved 19 December 2018, last reviewed 25 November 2024, review due 31 December 2026), 20 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC 4.0. eviQ also states that "eviQ content should not be hosted on external sites", and that commercial entities must contact eviQ to seek permission (read at https://www.eviq.org.au/copyright (Disclaimer and copyright, last updated 16 February 2022)). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) with Asian oncology societies (Lee, Menis et al.), ESMO Open 9 (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.103996) 'Pan-Asian adapted ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with oncogene-addicted metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer' (published 29 November 2024), 9 claims; LICENCE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (read at Europe PMC fullTextXML <license> element for PMC11648200). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Edition 2.0 adds S2, the Pan-Asian adaptation of the ESMO guideline for oncogene-addicted metastatic NSCLC (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, paraphrased and hash-anchored), for the EGFR-mutant treatment sequence (first-line options beyond osimertinib alone, uncommon and exon 20 mutations, resistance and later lines), which the single eviQ protocol (S1) does not give. Only S2's EGFR section is used. S1 claims and anchors are unchanged. The two PBS amivantamab rows are added to the PBS table because S2 now covers amivantamab.

claims.claim: **Osimertinib is first-line palliative therapy for locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC carrying an activating EGFR mutation.** It is also a second-line option once a T790M mutation is confirmed after progression on a first-generation EGFR TKI.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Non small cell lung cancer locally advanced or metastatic osimertinib (eviQ ID 1996 v.5)', ID 1996 v.5; first approved 19 December 2018, last reviewed 25 November 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1996, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **It also has a place after chemoradiation:** unresectable stage III NSCLC with an activating EGFR mutation that has not progressed after platinum-based chemoradiation.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Non small cell lung cancer locally advanced or metastatic osimertinib (eviQ ID 1996 v.5)', ID 1996 v.5; first approved 19 December 2018, last reviewed 25 November 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1996, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Test EGFR in advanced non-squamous NSCLC with a method that covers exons 18 to 21,** including resistance mutations [I, A].
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) with Asian oncology societies (Lee, Menis et al.), ESMO Open 9 (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.103996), 'Pan-Asian adapted ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with oncogene-addicted metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer', published 29 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11648200/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Classical EGFR mutations (exon 19 deletion or L858R): a third-generation TKI such as osimertinib is preferred first line, especially with brain metastases** [I, A]. First- or second-generation TKIs (erlotinib, gefitinib, afatinib, dacomitinib) remain single-agent alternatives.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) with Asian oncology societies (Lee, Menis et al.), ESMO Open 9 (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.103996), 'Pan-Asian adapted ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with oncogene-addicted metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer', published 29 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11648200/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Osimertinib plus carboplatin–pemetrexed is another first-line option** [I, A]. In FLAURA2 median PFS was 25.5 v 16.7 months with osimertinib alone (HR 0.62), at the cost of more grade 3 or worse events (64% v 27%), mostly anaemia and neutropenia.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) with Asian oncology societies (Lee, Menis et al.), ESMO Open 9 (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.103996), 'Pan-Asian adapted ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with oncogene-addicted metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer', published 29 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11648200/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Lazertinib plus amivantamab is a further first-line option** [I, A]. In MARIPOSA median PFS was 23.7 v 16.6 months against osimertinib (HR 0.70) and overall survival HR 0.77, but grade 3 or worse events rose to 75% from 43%, with more rash, paronychia, hypoalbuminaemia, peripheral oedema and venous thromboembolism.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) with Asian oncology societies (Lee, Menis et al.), ESMO Open 9 (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.103996), 'Pan-Asian adapted ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with oncogene-addicted metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer', published 29 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11648200/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Other first-line choices:** gefitinib with carboplatin–pemetrexed [I, B], or erlotinib with bevacizumab or ramucirumab [I, B], which lengthened PFS without a clear survival gain. For major uncommon (non-exon 20) sensitising mutations, use afatinib or osimertinib.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) with Asian oncology societies (Lee, Menis et al.), ESMO Open 9 (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.103996), 'Pan-Asian adapted ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with oncogene-addicted metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer', published 29 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11648200/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **EGFR exon 20 insertion: amivantamab with platinum chemotherapy first line** [I, A], or later [III, B]; in PAPILLON median PFS was 11.4 v 6.7 months (HR 0.40). Amivantamab alone is an option after platinum failure if not already used.
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) with Asian oncology societies (Lee, Menis et al.), ESMO Open 9 (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.103996), 'Pan-Asian adapted ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with oncogene-addicted metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer', published 29 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11648200/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Osimertinib 80 mg by mouth once daily**, continued until the disease progresses or toxicity becomes unacceptable. It is PBS authority-listed; 40 mg and 80 mg tablets exist.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Non small cell lung cancer locally advanced or metastatic osimertinib (eviQ ID 1996 v.5)', ID 1996 v.5; first approved 19 December 2018, last reviewed 25 November 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1996, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If a strong CYP3A4 inducer** (such as carbamazepine, phenytoin or rifampicin) **must be used, consider raising the dose to 160 mg once daily** and watch for toxicity; drop back to 80 mg 3 weeks after the inducer is stopped.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Non small cell lung cancer locally advanced or metastatic osimertinib (eviQ ID 1996 v.5)', ID 1996 v.5; first approved 19 December 2018, last reviewed 25 November 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1996, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No dose change is needed for kidney function** (use with caution when eGFR is below 15) **or for mild to moderate liver impairment;** osimertinib is not recommended in severe hepatic impairment.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Non small cell lung cancer locally advanced or metastatic osimertinib (eviQ ID 1996 v.5)', ID 1996 v.5; first approved 19 December 2018, last reviewed 25 November 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1996, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tablets are swallowed whole.** If swallowing is hard, disperse the tablet in 50 mL of plain water (no other liquid), drink it straight away and rinse the glass; the same method works through a nasogastric tube with 15 mL volumes, all given within 30 minutes.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Non small cell lung cancer locally advanced or metastatic osimertinib (eviQ ID 1996 v.5)', ID 1996 v.5; first approved 19 December 2018, last reviewed 25 November 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1996, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A missed or vomited dose is not made up;** skip a forgotten dose if the next one is due in under 12 hours.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Non small cell lung cancer locally advanced or metastatic osimertinib (eviQ ID 1996 v.5)', ID 1996 v.5; first approved 19 December 2018, last reviewed 25 November 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1996, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Blood tests at baseline, then monthly:** calcium, magnesium, phosphate, FBC, EUC/eGFR and LFTs.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Non small cell lung cancer locally advanced or metastatic osimertinib (eviQ ID 1996 v.5)', ID 1996 v.5; first approved 19 December 2018, last reviewed 25 November 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1996, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Check the heart before starting, especially with known cardiovascular disease:** ECG and relevant biochemistry, plus an echocardiogram in higher-risk patients. Repeat when clinically indicated or when a QT-prolonging drug is added.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Non small cell lung cancer locally advanced or metastatic osimertinib (eviQ ID 1996 v.5)', ID 1996 v.5; first approved 19 December 2018, last reviewed 25 November 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1996, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hepatitis B:** it is unknown whether routine HBsAg, anti-HBc and anti-HBs screening is needed with kinase inhibitors; decide case by case.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Non small cell lung cancer locally advanced or metastatic osimertinib (eviQ ID 1996 v.5)', ID 1996 v.5; first approved 19 December 2018, last reviewed 25 November 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1996, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **QTc prolongation:** if QTc is 500 ms or more on at least 2 separate ECGs, withhold until it is under 481 ms (or back to baseline), then restart at 40 mg. Stop permanently if QTc prolongation comes with signs of serious arrhythmia.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Non small cell lung cancer locally advanced or metastatic osimertinib (eviQ ID 1996 v.5)', ID 1996 v.5; first approved 19 December 2018, last reviewed 25 November 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1996, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis:** fatal ILD has occurred in 0.3% of osimertinib-treated patients, and radiation pneumonitis may be more frequent. The product information advises stopping for good; the treating clinician may still consider reintroduction.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Non small cell lung cancer locally advanced or metastatic osimertinib (eviQ ID 1996 v.5)', ID 1996 v.5; first approved 19 December 2018, last reviewed 25 November 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1996, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Keratitis:** refer promptly to ophthalmology for new or worsening eye inflammation, watering, photophobia, blurred vision, eye pain or a red eye. Contact lens wear may add risk.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Non small cell lung cancer locally advanced or metastatic osimertinib (eviQ ID 1996 v.5)', ID 1996 v.5; first approved 19 December 2018, last reviewed 25 November 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1996, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Acneiform rash is common and tends to peak in weeks 2 to 4.** Advise moisturiser and sunscreen; early or prophylactic doxycycline (a tetracycline) with 1% hydrocortisone cream can be considered.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Non small cell lung cancer locally advanced or metastatic osimertinib (eviQ ID 1996 v.5)', ID 1996 v.5; first approved 19 December 2018, last reviewed 25 November 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1996, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Diarrhoea:** loperamide is usually supplied. For grade 3 or 4 diarrhoea, hold osimertinib until it settles to grade 2 or less; if that takes no more than 3 weeks, restart at 80 mg or 40 mg, otherwise stop permanently.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Non small cell lung cancer locally advanced or metastatic osimertinib (eviQ ID 1996 v.5)', ID 1996 v.5; first approved 19 December 2018, last reviewed 25 November 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1996, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Interactions:** osimertinib inhibits BCRP and P-gp, so levels of drugs such as rosuvastatin, methotrexate, digoxin or clopidogrel can rise (watch for myopathy with rosuvastatin). Other QT-prolonging drugs, such as antiarrhythmics, antipsychotics, azoles, clarithromycin, methadone or ondansetron, add to the risk of torsades.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Non small cell lung cancer locally advanced or metastatic osimertinib (eviQ ID 1996 v.5)', ID 1996 v.5; first approved 19 December 2018, last reviewed 25 November 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1996, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **FLAURA (first line):** 556 patients with exon 19 deletion or L858R disease were randomised to osimertinib or to gefitinib or erlotinib. Median overall survival was 38.6 versus 31.8 months (HR 0.80).
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Non small cell lung cancer locally advanced or metastatic osimertinib (eviQ ID 1996 v.5)', ID 1996 v.5; first approved 19 December 2018, last reviewed 25 November 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1996, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **FLAURA toxicity:** grade 3 or worse adverse events in 42% on osimertinib and 47% on the older TKIs; rash or acne, diarrhoea and dry skin were the commonest.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Non small cell lung cancer locally advanced or metastatic osimertinib (eviQ ID 1996 v.5)', ID 1996 v.5; first approved 19 December 2018, last reviewed 25 November 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1996, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **AURA3 (second line, T790M-positive):** median progression-free survival 10.1 months with osimertinib against 4.4 months with platinum plus pemetrexed.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Non small cell lung cancer locally advanced or metastatic osimertinib (eviQ ID 1996 v.5)', ID 1996 v.5; first approved 19 December 2018, last reviewed 25 November 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1996, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **LAURA (after chemoradiation):** in 216 patients, median PFS was 39.1 months with osimertinib and 5.6 months with placebo (HR 0.16). The cost was more grade 3+ adverse events (35% vs 12%) and frequent radiation pneumonitis (48% vs 38%).
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, 'Non small cell lung cancer locally advanced or metastatic osimertinib (eviQ ID 1996 v.5)', ID 1996 v.5; first approved 19 December 2018, last reviewed 25 November 2024, review due 31 December 2026, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/1996, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Progression on a first- or second-generation TKI:** T790M-positive disease should get a third-generation TKI such as osimertinib second line [I, A]; T790M-negative disease may be treated with platinum chemotherapy [III, A]. A third-generation TKI can be considered for progression confined to the brain [III, B].
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) with Asian oncology societies (Lee, Menis et al.), ESMO Open 9 (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.103996), 'Pan-Asian adapted ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with oncogene-addicted metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer', published 29 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11648200/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **After progression on osimertinib: platinum–pemetrexed with amivantamab is the standard** [I, A]; platinum-doublet chemotherapy alone remains an option [III, B], and trials are encouraged, especially with a targetable resistance mechanism. In the pivotal trial (MARIPOSA2) median PFS was 6.3 v 4.2 months (HR 0.48). Consider plasma or tissue NGS at resistance [III, C].
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) with Asian oncology societies (Lee, Menis et al.), ESMO Open 9 (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.103996), 'Pan-Asian adapted ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with oncogene-addicted metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer', published 29 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11648200/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **After EGFR TKI failure, platinum with paclitaxel or pemetrexed plus an anti-PD-(L)1 antibody and bevacizumab may be considered** where neither drug class is contraindicated [III, B]. Checkpoint inhibitor monotherapy is only for after both TKIs and chemotherapy [IV, C].
claims.locator: European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) with Asian oncology societies (Lee, Menis et al.), ESMO Open 9 (doi 10.1016/j.esmoop.2024.103996), 'Pan-Asian adapted ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines for the diagnosis, treatment and follow-up of patients with oncogene-addicted metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer', published 29 November 2024, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11648200/, retrieved 2026-09-24
